entries.boundary: The replay profile checkpoints the original R060 resident status transaction after three data bits of its first request byte, after the independently checked streaming prefix completes. Two complete original-firmware continuations consume eleven RX bytes, emit the same fourteen TX bytes and empty the transaction queues without retry. At the identical worker-window endpoint all 1039 registered emulation-state items match byte-for-byte, including CPU, RAM, NAND, DMA, codec, McBSP, external peer and emulation timers. Nine Lua frontend resume-timer fields are explicitly excluded because MAME's Lua post-load callback resets that timer; no Lua script runs in this fixture. This establishes native status-transaction continuation, not arbitrary boot checkpoints, a native reset lifecycle, physical board attachment, processing or music playback

The pins profile drives original R060 status-request and acknowledgement bytes through McBSP2 frame, data and clock inputs with explicit 5us bench half-clock edges. It delegates native DRR and indexed control reads to the shared device rather than writing RRDY or pulsing CPU IRQ6. Device-owned RSR/RBR/DRR publication generates eleven receive interrupts, after which original firmware drains all eleven bytes and transmits the same fourteen-byte acknowledged status transaction without retry or queued residue. The 20-second window observes 1779 worker entries and 1780 clears with mode zero and no illegal instruction. Coverage is externally framed single-phase 8-bit delay-one ingress in this original resident lifecycle, not native transport save/replay, physical board clock/wiring, other formats, loader ingress replacement, music processing or full MU4 boot

Original initializer 03:9b07 configures indexed McBSP2 as externally clocked single-phase 8-bit with data delay one. Separate wire fixtures attach shared TX device registers, drive explicit 5us half-clock edges and deliver device-owned XRDY interrupts through IFR bit 7; original 02:8bfe drains TX indices and busy flags. An independent TX-bit consumer verifies each reported byte. The decoded 0x49 request produces original acknowledgement 7f0155 and response 1e05aa0171010000804055. With no peer acknowledgement the firmware transmits three identical response copies (36 bytes total). With register/IRQ peer acknowledgement 7f8055 it settles RX indices 11/11, TX indices 14/14, empty typed queue, cleared response pending and mode zero with no retry or illegal instruction. The acknowledged 20-second window observes 1779 worker entries and 1780 clears, not a replacement for the unchanged startup control. RX remains register-level bench ingress, clock rate and GPIO-to-frame relation are explicit bench inputs, and DXR reads expose bench write history. Complete board serial attachment, pin-level RX, native music and full MU4 boot remain unvalidated

Original R060 ISR 02:8ba9 reads register 0031 into the 80-word ring at 1462 with producer 1657. Parser 03:9dc7 consumes with index 1658 via eight-state table 02:4113; the normal path checks start 0x1e, length 1..79, header 0xaa, payload, separate sequence token and XOR including the token. A new token with matching XOR appends type-2 payload through 03:9b6d; a repeated token acknowledges without another command. The subsequent trailing word is unchecked. Processing reader 03:9f5e requests that type for dispatcher 03:acf2. Responses append type 1 and use TX ring 14b2, indices 1659/165a and register 0033. Literal far-call coverage over 48261 final uploaded program words finds four append sites and one processing-reader call, not indirect-call or overlay closure. The unchanged 20-second fixture executes parser/reader/dispatcher 174 times each and dequeue 348 times but no append or TX-word enqueue; both ring index pairs and queued-word count stay zero. The command control fixture supplies 1e02aa014901ff55 through register ingress/IRQ6; firmware drains all eight bytes, queues one command, constructs three acknowledgement words and writes 007f to storage-only TX register history, leaving TX indices 3/1 and four queued words. That control profile does not consume the selector. Separate wire fixtures validate device-owned TX completion and original query response; they do not establish physical board attachment or playback. No command memory, mode or callback is injected

The unchanged R060 startup fixture visits original worker 02:9545 1739 times in 20 seconds but all 1739 mode-gate branches at 02:954f skip buffer processing because bb80 remains zero. Later flag gates and transfer entry have zero visits; the only observed mode write is original initialization at 02:9099. Static processing requires bb80 nonzero and 94de/0062 zero. Original dispatcher 03:acf2 reads a queue into b9d2 through 03:9f5e and selects from program tables 02:40f5 and 02:4109; selectors 0x40/0x42/0x43 reach mode-1/mode-3/parameter-dependent mode-2 branches. A 48261-word program literal census has 17 bb80 matches and eight immediate-store candidates, not a complete dynamic-writer proof. Queue producers, physical host framing and decoded music remain unvalidated; no firmware state or command injection is used

SPRU172C p. 4-65 encodes INTR K as f7c0..f7df. It pushes the following PC, selects IPTR:4*K, sets INTM, clears the selected maskable IFR bit where applicable, ignores IMR and prior INTM and costs three cycles. XPC is retained. Sixty-four executable red/green cases cover all encodings with INTM clear/set, IMR zero, two vector bases, exact stack/PC/page/status/IFR outcomes and port-measured timing. Core and ROM4 warm/cold regressions pass. VC5410A SPRS139I table 3-21 identifies K=25 as HPI interrupt/SINT9: original MU4 f7d9 at 02:9c74 selects vector 2064, whose original branch targets 02:9a32. This is instruction/dispatch correctness, not proven native audio or a physical host transaction

SPRU131G 7.5.5.1 table 7-9 gives one-cycle SP latency from ordinary POPM, PSHM and FRAME to category-I compiler-mode direct addressing; extended-shift operands (category II) see updated SP. The core retains a saved preceding-SP DAGEN snapshot for this implemented producer group while architectural SP updates normally. Executable red/green conformance covers all three producers, immediate versus NOP-separated basic and extended-shift stores, and CPL clear/set (24 variants). Native MU4 timer context now places 4044 at reserved stack slot 127a and resumes 02:6d4e rather than corrupting XPC/PC. This is not complete DAGEN timing: other table-7-9 producer groups, longer SP-write latencies and interrupt-overlap hazards remain unvalidated

SPRU172C pp. 4-133--4-134 encodes RC ALT as fc43: test signed 40-bit A, pop the return PC and increment SP only when negative, leaving XPC unchanged. Original MU4 executes it at 02:3e44 after the timer-context latency correction. Five executable red/green cases cover minus one, minimum signed 40-bit value, zero, one and maximum positive value, exact PC/SP outcomes and page preservation. Core and ROM4 warm/cold fixtures pass. Complete native application or speech execution is not established

Startup 6d4b enables IMR bit 3 with IFR=0438; vector 204c branches to original 02:3d73 before the helper reaches 3f1d. Context code has POPM BL at 3d9e followed by basic CPL-relative STL A,6 at 3d9f. SPRU131G 7.5.5.1 table 7-9 requires one-instruction SP latency: preceding SP=1274 places continuation 4044 in reserved slot 127a rather than overwriting saved XPC at 127b. Implemented latency and executable red/green tests produce stack 4044,0002,6d4e at RET and resume original 02:6d4e. With INTR implemented, subsequent native execution passes its 20-second worker-activation gate. This is not full native application boot or validated music. Extension fetches are not independently treated as instructions. No stack word, mask, callback or firmware event is forced

SPRU302B sections 2.3.7.4 and 2.3.7.1 specify TX underflow and RX overrun. Supported external single-phase 8/12/16-bit framing repeats old DXR on new FSX with XEMPTY low; reset with no data transmits zero. Fresh DXR clears empty only on shifter transfer; refill alone does not resume a mid-frame underflow. Three unread RX words set RFULL while retaining DRR and RBR; later RSR input may be lost. Side-effectful DRR reads and receiver reset clear RFULL, debugger peeks do not. Executable fixtures validate bit order, ready-edge counts, recovery, reset and save/restore of partial TX and overrun RX state. Test phases yield to drain synchronized CPU input events. Wider, internally clocked and multichannel modes and physical timing remain outside this contract

Original 03:bb7b CMPR compares ordinal AR2 against AR0=0200: the iterator bound is 512 entries. At ordinal six, common byte-reader 329d receives A=0001:e9ff and offsets 00c0 through 00cb, matching a 32-byte entry. The observed cache loop advances its word count from zero to 0060, then reuses the cached position for subsequent bytes. Common 3035 increments address 0001:e9ff to 0001:ea00; actual opcode 5700 at 3050 loads the double-word stack operand into B, and the address builder emits the corresponding byte lanes correctly. This path is neither a proven unbounded iterator nor a defective address builder. Physical row advancement is not iterator advancement; the remaining operation is later settings-file initialization. No index limit, end record, filename content or firmware state is injected

Side-effect-free five-second startup snapshots leave raw pairs 142c/142d and 145c/145d at 0001,e9ff; 145e changes from zero to six. Last NAND strobes show column 00 and row bytes 02,e9,01 at the start, then column 00 and row bytes 98,e9,01 at the end: rows 01e902 and 01e998 in the validated small-page controller grammar. Reads increase from 259188 to 1164331. This proves later physical rows are reached during startup, not monotonic directory traversal or byte-cursor semantics. Child-call tracing separately proves the track-list lookup returns; later NAND activity cannot all be attributed to an outstanding lookup. No unverified track-list or settings-file content is generated

Original main 02:904b executes once but continuation 6dbf, helper 6d44 and selection start 3f1d have zero fetches in the bounded observation tails. Parent call 02:90f4 to 03:9105 remains outstanding; its child TRACKLST.BIN lookup at 03:9220 to 03:bcb6 returns, as proven by subsequent call 03:922c to 03:941d. That file-handling routine also returns, followed by returned calls to 03:90d6 and 03:8be6. The last observed parent call is 03:9282 to 03:8c3e for SETTING1.BIN initialization. An outstanding parent does not establish an outstanding lookup. The five-second tail completes 3453 TX/RX blocks with 905143 NAND reads, illegal=0, zero consumer entries and zero b633 reads; only the first 1024 TX words are independently compared to DIN. No full native application boot, music decoding or settings-write completion is established; no firmware state, file contents or hardware input is forced

Original C initialization populates descriptor 16b8 with SETTING followed by a space and extension BIN. Parent code replaces the last name character with ASCII 0031, 0032 and 0033 for SETTING1.BIN, SETTING2.BIN and SETTING3.BIN; 0031 is not a service-command tag. The observed first call 03:9282 to 03:8c3e supplies a 001c-word payload. In the five-second scan, directory iteration finishes with the name comparison returning -1 and bb4e returning 1. Subsequent bb09, bfdb and both c2c2 calls return; the first c2c2 receives length 001c, the second zero. Call 03:8cb9 to 03:c404 remains outstanding at the observation boundary. Static c404 code updates a directory-entry buffer and invokes further storage helpers. Its metadata finalization/allocation contract, persistent-file format and full application behavior remain unresolved. Snapshots are pre-execution; AR2 at a return site is not automatically the returned result. No settings file, callback, firmware state or hardware event is injected

In the five-second original scan, outstanding c404 returns from bd13, c57f, b91d and b9ae before calling c4c7 at 03:c44f. In c4c7, common 345c and 2096 calls return. The first observed 03:c552 call to c5b2 with input address 0001:e901 returns; the next with 0001:e980 remains outstanding. An earlier c404 invocation completes through the same helpers, so no uniformly non-returning routine is established. Static c5b2 uses b3f8 as a block buffer and b4f8 as a cached address, invokes read/flush helpers and performs filesystem-mode-specific masked updates. The active internal branch and completion condition remain unresolved; a bounded observation is not a deadlock proof. All probes are side-effect-free and no media, firmware state or input is forced

The original five-second scan selects filesystem mode 1 in c5b2: runtime CMPR operands are AR2=1 against AR0=4 at c5f3, then against AR0=1 at c5f8; c5fb invalid-mode loop has no observed fetch. Initial c5ea calls to c57f return for addresses 0001:e901 and 0001:e980. Execution reaches c6ad and final child calls: earlier c6ba to b91d and c6bd to b9ae return. In the active SETTING1.BIN operation, the final c6ba call to b91d with cached address 0001:e980 has no observed return within five seconds. The unresolved boundary is this buffer/flush preparation path, not mode selection or initial cache loading. No deadlock, failed program verification, native music or complete application boot is established. Routine probes must include the final section beyond c6ad. No firmware state, file content or device input is forced

TI SPRU172C pp. 4-70--4-71 syntax 3 encodes LD #k9,DP as ea00..ebff, replacing only ST0 bits 8--0 in one cycle. Original MU4 startup executes ea00 at 02:3d7e after storage initialization. The previously unsupported encoding is implemented and executable conformance checks all 512 immediate values in two CPL/SXM configurations, preservation of other ST0/ST1 bits and both accumulators, and one-cycle timing between two-cycle port probes. Core conformance and existing warm/cold ROM4 fixtures pass. This is an ISA contract, not a claim of complete native application or speech execution

In the five-second settings-buffer scope, c57f has 57 calls and 56 returns; page-program/readback-verification helpers have zero observed calls. Static b91d loops over 32 page reads. The separate startup profile observes storage initialization returning, main completing and startup-helper entry. With specified SP-address latency, RC ALT and INTR implemented, the complete 20-second gate passes with illegal=0, consumer 02:9545 entries=1739, b633 reads=1739 and clears=1740, final pending=0. TX/RX DMA completions are 13789/13789 and startup continuation/helper/selection-start counts are 1/1/7. Only the initial 1024 DIN words are independently compared; neither transfer volume nor consumer activity proves music correctness. Physical 1820 is a harness-installed loader-return IDLE sentinel, not a firmware idle loop. The open boundary is the consumer's host-command/data contract and verified output. No missing peer, settings file or firmware state is synthesized; this is not full native boot or music decoding

Original common code uses DP 017b with CPL clear: direct operand base bd80, not low peripherals. Short worker-window observations give bdb8=0001, bdb9=0010, bde3=0000, bde4=8028 and bde7=3da6. At 3f5b A=-15 makes AGT false; at 3f5f A=0001000000 from bdbc=1 makes ALT false. Original TX ISR increments bdbc at 02:8b0d..8b0e and decrements it at 02:8b52..8b53; initialization leaves it zero. Common tail actually executes RET at 3da6. Short-window paged epilogue probes observe TC clear after BITF 8000 at 02:8b54 and BC NTC at 02:8b56 taking ordinary epilogue 02:8b6d, not deferred return-word replacement 02:8b63. These are window-scoped observations, not closure of all selection paths. Static startup helper 6d44 calls 3f1d at 6d5e; entry calls that helper at 6dbf after far call 02:904b. The complete 20-second startup gate observes seven selection-start entries and 1739 original consumer entries. Official queue/priority identities and complete application lifecycle remain unresolved; no firmware state or hardware event is injected

Original 02:6d89 populates data object 806e, including 8074=0002 and 8075=9545, an address pair matching the candidate consumer entry 02:9545. Worker acceptance checks the pair and separately counts actual entry fetches. Common code at 02:3f41 writes the first object word to zero; 02:3f57 writes 8071=802b. Endpoint prefix is 0000,bdc8,0010,802b,0000,0000,0002,9545. Original writes at 002fa8/02:6d89/02:6d0d leave data 007e=4000; common routines test masks c001/c020. The uninitialized-object/word hypothesis is falsified, but selection/resume semantics and official task/priority/stack identity remain unresolved. No object field, callback or firmware state is forced

Original TX ISR writes b633=1, loads AR2=806e and calls common routines 3f37/3ec2. Original 02:9549 reads b633 and branches to 02:9676 when zero; 02:9641 clears it. This is an inferred software-notification role, not an official task identity or audio-decoding claim. A separate worker profile runs a verified 100 ms tail after eight-block acceptance: 9844 TX words, 77 TX completions/handler entries, 76 RX completions, illegal=0 at 00306c. Only the first 1024 TX words are checked against codec DIN. Read-only observers see 77 ISR sets, one initialization clear, zero firmware reads and final b633=1; final inspection is side-effect-free. The consumer lifecycle/806e descriptor remains unresolved; no callback, readiness or firmware state is injected

Original TX vector 206c contains 4a1e,f495,f882,8afc and branches to logical 02:8afc. Read-only fetch observers exclude program-table/DMA/debugger reads; eight-block sustain acceptance requires at least seven original vector and handler entries, allowing the last completion still to be pending. Observed IMR 0ac1 enables source 11 but masks source 10: eight RX blocks complete without RX vector entry and IFR bit 10 remains pending. IMR/IFR observations use CPU state, not direct AS_DATA reads bypassing internal MMR access. This proves repeated native TX interrupt delivery, not complete application startup, RX interrupt ownership, analog conversion, music processing or playback

The separate sustain BIOS executes unchanged original MCUSI16 beyond the first digital block. It verifies 1024 transmitted words against codec DIN channel/value ordering, eight TX DMA completions, eight RX DMA completions and the reloaded RX destination 1900/1940 containing explicitly converted fixture samples 1234/5678. Codec clocks and pins, not injected DRR/readiness or firmware-buffer writes, drive the run. Original six control words remain unchanged and CPU illegal=0 at PC 003080. Eight blocks cover 512 stereo frames (about 11.6 ms), not long-duration application behavior, analog conversion, meaningful music samples, playback or native telephony

Generic external rx_data_w/rx_clock_w/rx_frame_w capture single-phase 8/12/16-bit words. TI SPRU302B defines sampled frame detection, clock polarity, RDATDLY, frame length/ignore, RSR-to-RBR opposite-edge transfer and next sampling-edge DRR/RRDY publication. DRR1 consumption clears saved REVT level; debugger peeks do not. Unread DRR retains its word while RBR holds the next. RJUST formats zero/sign extension or left alignment. Executable fixtures cover no-frame stalls, early-frame ignore, edge handoffs, two-word buffering, widths, delays 0/1/2, both polarities, justification, peeks, RRST cancellation, RINT0 and partial-word save/replay after synchronization drains. Overrun recovery, dual phase, wider words, companding, nonzero RINTM, loopback/SPI/A-bis receive and active format changes fail explicitly when exercised; internal receive generation/reset activation remain unvalidated. This is pin/MMIO conformance, not native codec ADC reception

A physical-pin fixture using original RX RCR=0140/0044 PCR=000e delivers 1234/5678 through McBSP0 DRR1 and REVT0 to DMA channel 2. No ready event or DRR word is injected. Before readiness no DMA occurs; deferred reads consume DRR, clear readiness and sort destination 6300/6340 using DMIDX0/DMFRI0. One two-word block verifies bank 2e..31 auto-reload and INTOSEL=1 maps DMA2 completion to CPU IFR bit 10. Generic RINT0 independently maps bit 4. Coupled codec/DMA save-replay and original 64-frame converted-sample RX have separate coverage. Analog codec ADC, physical bus arbitration and complete mux/sustained duplex remain unvalidated

Partial AIC23 control-word input stores the seven-bit-address/nine-bit-data grammar, reset defaults and activation/power/master gates. Observed USB/272 16-bit DSP LRP=1 mode generates BCLK=MCLK and a one-bit frame pulse every 272 clocks; CLKIN divides the codec, CLKOUT is independent of BCLK. DIN samples on rising BCLK; frame/DOUT changes follow falling BCLK. DOUT serializes an explicitly required already-converted stereo callback, not an analog ADC or implicit silence source. The coupled codec/McBSP/DMA fixture verifies 1104 rising edges in 92 microseconds, frame spacing, raw DIN words, converted-sample RX, reset and exact ten-microsecond mid-word replay. Detailed logical timing is sourced from related AIC23B figures 2-2/3-8, with original AIC23 EVM corroborating port split and master DSP framing. SPI pins, analog conversion, other active master formats and revision-specific electrical timing remain unimplemented or unvalidated

Generic McBSP tx_clock_w/tx_frame_w inputs implement externally clocked single-phase 8/12/16-bit frames. TI SPRU302B defines polarity, opposite-edge XRDY, frame length/ignore and asynchronous zero-delay first bit. Executable ordered-pin tests cover frame gating, two-word MSB-first output, ignored early frame, zero/one/two-bit delays, both polarities, readiness edge, reset cancellation and mid-word save/replay. Same-time asynchronous first-bit and clock events do not shift twice. Save/load checkpoints wait for synchronized CPU input events to drain and assert scheduler can_save; anonymous input-drain timers are not restored. XINT0 must be latched in CPU IFR bit 5 before save and after restore. These are logical edge tests, not electrical timing measurements. Underrun and unexpected-frame recovery without XFIG explicitly fail. External receive has separate subset coverage; active TX reconfiguration and full reset-activation timing remain unvalidated. Original stream transmits one 128-word DMA block with codec-generated clocks; this is not ADC/DAC conversion or playback acceptance

Original loaded MCUSI16 programs channel 2 at logical 02:9854..9894: source 0021, destination 1980, count 0001, sync 103f, mode c055, per-channel reload 2e..31 values 0021,1900,0001,103f. TI maps 0021 to McBSP0 DRR1 and event 1 to REVT0. Mode fixes source and applies DMIDX0/DMFRI0 sorting to destination with two elements and 64 frames, auto-reload and block IRQ. This complements TX channel 3. Original stream acceptance observes channel-2 completion and all 128 sorted words at 1980/19c0 from explicit converted fixture samples 1234/5678 serialized through codec DOUT. No receive event or firmware buffer is injected. Analog codec ADC and sustained duplex remain unvalidated

NPM-5 MU4 schematic sheet 2 identifies U601 TLV320AIC23PW and 11.9952 MHz DSP_CLKOUT. Original controls decode power 10, analog 18, digital 01, format 53, sample-rate 23, active 01. Related TI AIC23B corroborates master/DSP/16-bit stereo and USB/272 clock selection; 11995200/272=44100. McBSP0 PCR=000e XCR=0140/0044 SRGR=0f07/101f SPCR2=0101 selects external framed two-word transmission with XFIG. Original AIC23 EVM corroborates the McBSP0 audio/McBSP1 control split. Stream observes 128 TX words verified against codec DIN, TX DMA completion and a complete original RX DMA block from explicitly supplied converted samples, with illegal=0 and no firmware forcing. The gate rejects input-queue overflow. Save/load checkpoints drain anonymous CPU synchronization timers before loading. Physical SPI decoding, analog ADC/DAC conversion, original-versus-B electrical timing, sustained duplex and playback remain unvalidated

McBSP XRDY publishes a saved-state-backed level callback separate from CPU interrupt pulses. DMA retains asserted sync levels and services readiness already high when DE is enabled. Executable conformance verifies pre-enable ready, held level without duplicate edge and re-enable. MU4 fixture attaches separate McBSP0/1 data/control ports and maps XEVT0/1 to DMA events 2/6. Partial INTOSEL mux suppresses XINT1 while DMA3 owns IFR bit 11; synthetic frame-transfer conformance checks CPU IFR ordering. External RX and its channel-2 composition have separate subset coverage; full mux, overlapping arbitration and codec conversion remain unvalidated; external framed TX and original finite TX block have separate coverage

Generic enhanced DMA implements event-gated single-word multiframe transfers, signed element/frame sorting indices, shared/per-channel auto-reload and block/frame callbacks. TI defines count/index/reload/event fields. MMIO tests verify event stalls, deferred sorted two-frame output, notification order, reload or DE clearance and pending save/replay. Two-clock cadence is assumed; ABU, double-word and overlapping arbitration fail explicitly. MU4 McBSP0 and partial interrupt/ready-line wiring have separate coverage. An original finite TX block has separate coverage; physical arbitration timing and codec conversion remain unvalidated

Original MCUSI16 writes DMA bank 32..35 at logical 02:9728..9735 with 1300,0023,0001,203f before enabling channel 3, confirming VC5410A per-channel reload layout. Generic DMA selects this variant explicitly; six banks, eight-bit frame masking, reserved 28/29 and bank save/restore have executable coverage. Auto-reload transfer mechanics are covered separately by c54x_dma_synchronized_multiframe_subset. One original finite TX block has separate coverage; sustained streaming and the channel-enable extension remain unvalidated

Original MCUSI16 configures channel 3 source 1300 destination 0023 count 0001 sync 203f mode c541 DMPREC 4848, DMIDX0=0040 DMFRI0=ffc1. TI identifies McBSP0 transmit sync, two elements/frame, 64 frames, fixed destination, sorting, block IRQ and auto-reload, not ABU. Source sequence is 1300,1340,1301,1341 through 133f,137f. VC5410A maps 0023 to McBSP0 DXR1 and INTOSEL=1 to DMA3 on IFR bit 11. Reload writes select 32..35. With original codec controls driving master clocks, 128 TX words and one DMA completion are observed with illegal=0; codec DIN independently verifies channel/value ordering of those words. Buffer contents are not validated music samples; converted-fixture RX has separate coverage and sustained operation remains unvalidated

Original MCUSI16 configures McBSP1 48/49 and transmits six words 0c10 0818 0a01 0e53 1023 1201 through a partial generic transmitter. TI defines XRST/XRDY/DXR/XSR and CPU/2 division. Fixtures cover 8/12/16-bit output, stall, buffering, cancellation, IRQ and save/restore; external framed TX has separate coverage. BITF displacement-before-mask is tested. Setup BIOS stops after the sixth word. Stream BIOS observes original finite TX and converted-fixture RX blocks through the codec digital interface. No physical PLL, analog conversion or playback completion is claimed

After exact original-loader destination verification, isolated mu4nand invokes unchanged InitData 3538 with descriptor index zero. Original firmware reloads MCUSI16, writes PMST 2028 and branches to program 2000; loaded code transfers to logical page 2 address 6d62. Read-only program-bus taps observe both entries. TI SPRU131G 3.2.5 specifies OVLY common lower 32K CPU accesses; physical page-zero words supplied by original DMA are used while logical XPC remains 2. DMA does not use the CPU overlay translation. Core fixtures cover overlay-on fetch/READA/WRITA, unique upper pages and overlay-off control/save/repeat tests. Original code exposes documented LD immediate ARP and LD Smem DP forms. Entry execution is not full startup, music playback or handset boot; DA150 RAM aliases, physical extents and peripherals remain unresolved

Isolated mu4nand mounts original-firmware-populated media and calls unchanged MCUSI16 loader 2ed4 with stack 3aea. Original 2f56 programs DMA 54..57 for asynchronous transfers. All 3254 records and 51921 destinations match independently decoded source in data/program spaces; SP balances and DE clears. Fixtures cover deferred completion, one-word count, page wrap, cancellation and pending save/restore. This loader exercises nonsynchronized single-frame transfers; broader DMA mechanics have separate conformance coverage. Two-clock cadence is unmeasured and physical memory/arbitration/PLL unresolved. InitDisk-only read-only mappings are removed on InitData restoration. Native entry has separate coverage; full MU4/handset boot remains unvalidated

On the medium populated only by original InitDisk and original serial ingress, original InitData mount 308e succeeds, directory routines 09c6/09fa/0a0b construct six named BIN descriptors and return end-of-directory. Original seek 33ea and reader 32d3 retrieve all 720268 file bytes in at most 256-word chunks. Exact source comparisons verify MCUSI16/aa22, MP3SI16/aa44, AACSI16/aabb, RERSI16/aa88, RELSI16/aa99 and USBSI16/aadd, names/extensions/lengths, unique markers and balanced-stack idle returns. Static 32dc name copies start at 0112 (descriptor index one), correcting the prior one-record name shift: aa55 is unnamed raw boot, bb77/bbcc name PRODINFO/TESTINFO. MCUSI16 starts with count/high/low 0010/0002/2000. No filesystem state or return success is injected. DMA completion, loader/program execution, host NVRAM persistence, full MU4 boot and native handset services remain unvalidated

After original InitDisk provisions erased NAND, isolated mu4nand supplies all 741916 original R060 container bytes through receive register 0031 and IRQ6 at test-only 1ms cadence, pausing on external XF busy. Unchanged ISR, ring consumer, seven marker selections, raw/file write paths and payload-only XOR comparisons execute; final checksum is 0040, state zero and ring drained. Original InitData mounts the retained populated medium successfully. Both acquired R060/R061 containers statically match payload-only checksum for all seven segments. Original 9488 in file writer independently exposes compact LD Xmem,SHFT,A; 16 core fixtures cover sign, destination, shifts and postincrement. Independent file-content readback, DMA-backed load, serial physical timing, full MU4 boot and native handset services remain unvalidated

Isolated mu4nand supplies independent erased NAND and clean test RAM, loads original InitDisk C globals, and executes unchanged 346a/30de(057e). Firmware scans and writes metadata then reaches its empty-ring receive loop with nine descriptors initialized, state/completion zero and no received words. After soft reset and original InitData library/global restoration, unchanged partition-aware 308e mount returns zero with balanced SP and NAND busy waits on the retained firmware-written medium. Original 6fe1/60e1 bytes independently correct long shifted Smem/CMPM extension ordering; carry C/NC branches have eight core fixtures. No disk image, BPB, directory or return success is injected. Firmware-file transfer, full MU4 boot, physical mapping/timing and native handset services remain unvalidated

Original InitDisk 0080 vectors branch from 00d8 to ISR 2b03, which reads 0031. TI VC5410A mapping corroborates McBSP2 DRR1, indexed 0034/0035 and RINT2 bit 6. Isolated mu4nand executes original 346a initialization, delivers two word-level receive inputs with RRDY/interrupts, observes original ISR populate its own ring and original 34c0 consume 1234 with balanced SP. Serial clocks/framing/overrun/DMA and MCU forwarding remain unvalidated. Original 32dc maps nine segment markers to unnamed raw aa55 plus eight named descriptors beginning at aa22; bbcc names TESTINFO. Provisioning, segment transfer and exact consumer file readback are separately covered; file-backed boot remains unvalidated

Isolated mu4nand near-calls unchanged InitDisk 36b9 with original C globals, context 068c and stack output pointers 2000/2100. Both original code records 256d and 4aa9 are loaded; helper 4aaf is required by metadata writeback. The call scans 4096 blocks, records the external block-zero bad marker, reports no bad reserved blocks, returns zero with balanced SP and leaves its 256-word bitmap byte-swapped by original writer 256d. The gate observes 156412 NAND reads and 37778 busy-pin reads. Missing 4aa9 explains prior wrapper re-entry, not a CPU loop defect. Full DA150 memory/timing, provisioning marker preservation, filesystem validity and serial host delivery remain unvalidated

Isolated mu4nand loads unchanged InitDisk code and original 2080 C globals, then near-calls 377a/2889 with block zero and context 0585. Erased first-two-page spare markers return ff; external NAND programming of page-zero spare byte 5 to zero makes the same original reader return zero after one page. Both require busy/status handling and balanced SP. Complete scan execution is separately validated by npm5_mu4_initdisk_scan_execution. No filesystem or full MU4/handset boot is claimed

Original InitDisk R060 30de calls 36b9, which scans 256 groups of 16 NAND blocks via 2889/2832. Command 50 reads 16 spare bytes on each block's first two pages; byte 5 must be ff on both for return ff, otherwise the group bitmap records a bad block. The final seven blocks are separately examined. Subsequent receive state machine consumes an 8-bit-wrapped RAM ring whose 2b03 interrupt writer reads peripheral register 0031; 35c7 configures indexed registers 0034/0035. This establishes a serial-peripheral ingress, not direct USB FIFO delivery. Scan execution is separately covered by npm5_mu4_initdisk_scan_execution; allocation semantics, exact DA150 serial/IRQ/clock, external sender and filesystem provisioning remain unvalidated

Original 0880 recovery writer, supplied only unchanged 0f33 C globals and routine ABI context, writes the exact 512-byte original template to logical sector 31/physical NAND row 32 through 069b/0725. Independent byte reads match it. Subsequent unchanged 051d remounts with flag zero, returns failure one and issues no erase/program on the still-missing boot record. Startup recovery alone is not erased-media provisioning; original InitDisk provisioning and consumer mount are now separately covered by npm5_mu4_original_erased_provisioning, while firmware-file population remains unresolved

Isolated mu4nand executes unchanged InitData R060 mount 308e through original 2080..20ad trampolines, with startup ABI context 3aea and partition-aware flag one. Erased boot-sector reads use GPIO/NAND/live BIO and return failure one with balanced SP. Original 6be6/76e1 context operations corroborate displacement-before-immediate ordering for long-offset ADDM and ST. No successful filesystem, directory population, file placement or full MU4/handset boot is claimed

Original InitData startup 09b5 selects descriptor zero and calls 2080->3538->2ed4 before a far branch to program 2000. A 44-word descriptor at data 36b0 feeds file readers 33ea/32d3; three one-word header reads yield count and 32-bit destination, payload is read to data 3c21, and 2f56 programs DMA 54/55/56 then polls completion. VC5410A family documentation corroborates DMPREC/DMSA/DMSDI and banked channel fields. Original firmware file population, exact consumer readback and all loaded destinations are covered by npm5_mu4_original_segment_transfer/npm5_mu4_original_file_readback/npm5_mu4_original_dma_loader. OVLY and isolated original program entry are covered by npm5_mu4_original_program_entry. Full DA150 DMA mapping/timing and full startup remain unvalidated; outer A00 segments are not this file stream

Isolated mu4nand fixture executes unchanged InitData R060 dirty-cache flush 0725 with declared ABI cache/base/dirty inputs. Original GPIO/BIO code erases block 2, programs 32 pages, writes ff spare fill and verifies each page against the cache. Independent device reads verify 8192 patterned words and 512 spare bytes; return zero, balanced SP, cleared dirty flag and preserved CPL are required. Test-only program/data maps, clock and ADD_H remain assumptions; no filesystem, full DA150 startup or handset boot is claimed

Isolated mu4nand fixture executes unchanged InitData R060 routines 3035 and 306c through an ordinary reset wrapper, GPIO 003c/003d, K9K1208U0A I/O and live BIO. Erased row 1 returns ffff; externally programmed row 65536 returns 3412 from bytes 12/34 after soft reset. Both require five command/address writes, two reads, a busy-pin wait and balanced SP. ADD_H is fixture-enabled and the clock/maps are test assumptions; this does not validate full DA150 startup, filesystem, overlay selection or handset boot

Core BIO callback reads the board pin, defaulting high when unconnected. SPRU172C defines BIO low/NBIO high. Executable conformance covers 28 pin-level variants of BC/BCD/CC/RC/RCD/XC plus a live busy-loop release. MU4 sheet 4 wires NAND R/B to DA150 BIO, but no handset currently executes that storage attachment; this validates CPU pin semantics rather than DA150 memory mapping or media provisioning

MU4 schematic sheets 4/7 identify U201 K9K1208U0A and U202 SN74LV138APWR. DSP R/W,A14,A15 select NAND Y2/Y3 strobes in I/O quadrant 0x4000..0x7fff and USB Y6/Y7 in 0xc000..0xffff subject to IOSTRB and ADD_H. HD0/HD1/HD2 connect CLE/ALE/CE; BIO connects NAND R/B, and HPIENA is grounded. Original 003d masks 1/2/4 command sequencing agrees with TI HPI-GPIO family registers 003c/003d. DA150 full peripheral mapping, address-enable ownership and media placement remain unresolved. This is schematic plus static-contract evidence, not board execution

Original InitData R060/R061 first-segment code reaches FAT-family mount routine 0x308e through trampoline 0x2082. Byte/word/dword readers resolve through 0x329d/0x3234/0x32ad to control-register 0x003d masks 1/2/4, I/O port 0x4000 and BIO waits. This is a static consumer contract, not validated NAND/controller behavior, media placement, overlay selection or native execution; MU4 music DSP remains distinct from the missing MAD2 baseband mask

The MAD2 ARM mask ROM is undumped; every locally available shared boot_rom file is uniform erased fill. Supported profiles execute a single ARM reset-vector branch to the cross-product flash entry 0x200040 through normal CPU reset/pipeline behavior, without forcing PC. Clock, power and flashing-mode setup remain outside the HLE, and NSE-3 does not borrow a later MAD revision
The extracted GENSIO device owns endpoint selection and ready/data-available status at 0x2d/0x6d; selected CCONT command/data bytes cross callbacks at 0x2c/0x6c and endpoint 0x25 resets command phase

3210 v6.00 and v5.01 share direct read/write use of SELECT latches 0x6f and 0xaf; 3410 v5.46 directly writes the distinct 0xad/0xae/0xed/0xee set, while the conservative census resolves no SELECT accesses in 3310 v6.39 or 3330 v4.50. Saved latch behavior is extracted, but attached board peripherals remain unidentified and unmodeled

3210 v6.00 and v5.01 share ten-bit ADC result registers and reset status. On v6.00, selector 5 is VCHAR: firmware routine 0x2b084c takes six samples and debounces presence around raw 0x64. Operational connection and removal route through MAD2 IRQ2, task-1 event 0x51 and policy 0x2b08c6; focused traces validate source-bit read, write-one-clear acknowledgement, cleared status and settled controller state

VCHAR present from reset selects task-1 mode 0x0009, whose handler at 0x2711fc accepts reports 0x0e and 0x02 rather than shutdown report 0x07 directly. A sustained physical power hold follows a separate controller/teardown route through mode 0x000c into acting-dead mode 0x0005. Post-power-off charger insertion now restarts the retained CCONT plus reset MAD2 domain through the separately validated charger-wake contract

The phone supplies eight deterministic raw ten-bit selector inputs and latches each conversion across separate result-byte reads. Both 3210 ROMs prove logical-source routing; Nokia board documentation identifies Vb/RSSI, Vdc_out/VBAT, Vchout/BSI, BTEMP, VCHAR, RF_temp/VCXOTEMP and EAD. Selector 1's internal NSE-8 mux, several transfer scales and physical battery dynamics remain unresolved

CCONT owns a deterministic binary RTC with ROM-mapped second, minute and alarm interrupt sources, plus the documented eight-bit seconds watchdog: every nonzero watchdog-register write reloads the byte value and zero requests power-down. WDDISX is a modeled physical input and the default 3210 profile leaves it released; both supported 3210 ROMs service the enabled watchdog organically

3210 v6.00 and v5.01 both read CCONT reset status 0x03: persistent ready bit 0 plus clearable PWRONX cause bit 1. The device owns this stored reset state; an explicit ready-low fault reproduces the CONTACT SERVICE failure frame without a read overlay

3210 v6.00 and v5.01 share a 4-row by 5-column scan; any unmasked physical column transition latches MAD2 IRQ0, while firmware mask writes suppress row-drive scan transitions. Press and release decode through the firmware 0x41/0x42/0x43 sequence; electrical debounce and unexercised timing remain provisional

3210 v6.00 and v5.01 share the live timer-0 divider, coherent 16-bit counter, counter-plus-two compare, FIQ4 assertion and write-one-clear acknowledgement contract; the physical input clock remains unproved

The extracted nokia_mad2_device owns CTSI offsets 0x00..0x16, reset/clock/watchdog latches, timer state, interrupt pending/masks, ARM IRQ/FIQ routing and read-only external-status input 0x0e. All five supported ROMs read 0x0e and contain zero direct writers; the 3210 tests bits 0..2 independently, but physical pin ownership remains unknown

3210 v6.00 and v5.01 share reset-cause reads, organic watchdog reloads of 0x31, and the peripheral clock-gate lifecycle 0x00-to-0x0c-to-0x2c-to-0x0c; the complete paired-ROM census assigns bit 1 to ARM clock-stop, bits 5-6 exclusively to SIMI routines and bits 2-3 to a boot-only common enable, while bit 4 has no writer; bit 5 drives the extracted SIMI clock callback, but bit 6, the bit-2/bit-3 consumers and physical transition timing remain unresolved

MAD2 retains IRQ/FIQ pending and mask state and aggregates modeled component sources onto ARM lines; focused fixtures validate simultaneous keypad IRQ0/CCONT IRQ2 without destructive acknowledgement, pending retention across masks, immediate delivery on unmask/global enable, and FIQ8 ninth-bit projection/mask/ack routing; both 3210 ROMs independently establish that the separate ninth IRQ is read at 0x0c.bit5 and acknowledged by writing bit 6, but its physical owner and several other line assignments remain unvalidated

The extracted nokia_mbus_device owns MAD2 PUP offsets 0x18..0x1a, RX/TX holding state and FIQ2/FIQ3 callbacks. The controller runs at the documented 9,600 baud; v6.00/v5.01 share receive-mode initialization and an external-byte fixture validates RX-ready, firmware consumption and FIQ2 acknowledgement. NAM-2 independently proves FIQ3-started physical TX, consumes physical single-wire TX echo and emits checksum-valid M2BUS registration; public terminal D0/04 makes firmware organically return D0/05. Exact FIQ3 phase, differing-line collision representation and the expected external endpoint remain unknown.
MCUIF retains the four boot-written bytes 6a 0f 61 20, but the fields and memory-window side effects are not decoded and the coherent run never reads them back

The extracted neutral UIF device owns saved latch banks 0x30..0x33, 0x70..0x73, 0xb0..0xb3 and 0xf0..0xf3 without invented pin effects. On 3210, offset 0x31 is a CTRL-I/O output latch whose recovered accesses are bit-1 read-modify-writes owned by the power duty-cycle subsystem; no external-input or interrupt behavior is established

The extracted nokia_simi_device owns MAD2 offsets 0x36..0x3f, 16-byte TX FIFO, RX queue, organic IIR causes 0x10/0x40, response cadence and FIQ6; decoded causes 0x02/0x20/0x80 are exposed only through an inactive typed fault ingress pending physical trigger evidence; control/status bit 3 reports active-high socket absence and live card-presence edges assert MAD2 FIQ7; it exchanges only activation and bytes with the separate card device

ATR, PPS and organically requested T=0 exchanges compose through SIMI and task 21 without firmware messages or RAM forcing; physical removal and reinsertion follow the recovered status-bit-3/FIQ7 contract across both 3210 ROMs, while fixed response delays and the physical sources/timing of decoded timeout/parity causes remain provisional

The default Phase-2 and opt-in CPHS/AoC profiles provide synthetic subscriber identity, service and file data for coherent firmware transactions; this is test provisioning rather than phone hardware behavior

Task 7 is strongly mapped as the firmware adapter for class-0x40 frames; the request-driven service/test session now has a separate device behind the DSP transport, while its vocabulary and calibrated sequencing remain boot-subset prototypes

The extracted DSPIF device owns shared RAM, DSPIF, packet framing and ring indices; MCU task 3 serializes outbound work and FIQ 0 owns inbound delivery. Complete TX consumption and RX publication are focused-tested, while wrap/full/fault behavior remains open

The DSP HLE publishes state into DSPIF-owned shared RAM rather than overriding reads: both 3210 ROMs complete 64 alternating 0x0fe/0x100 acknowledgements and 3310 v6.39 completes 58 before the product-configured peer publishes ready words 0x000..0x004; NHM-2 ping-pong, parked-loader word 0x002 and service code-block behavior are backend-owned, while DSPIF retains only RAM, rings, doorbells and address-level access notifications; command 4 clears busy word 0x0e0, no DSP core executes, and physical response timing remains unknown

Matched 20-second v5.01/v6.00 runs expose the same 125 firmware-read byte offsets. All reachable reads are classified as self-test/bootstrap, shared-control, packet-ring indices or peer-produced RX contents; no phone-side synthesized read remains. Offset 0x0dc is a mapped shared-control request/completion word but no later completion-dependent read is reached

Matched 20-second v5.01/v6.00 runs reduce the active DSP-owned scalar contract to the same nine offsets with relocated matching consumers. Service pending 0x0e4 is request-triggered and one-shot; removing about 4,955 idle zero-to-zero IRQ4 completions per ROM preserves the transport and interactive-menu gates. Bootstrap word 0x004 is published but has no post-bootstrap reader in either run

Matched 20-second v5.01/v6.00 traces each contain 34 outbound and 11 inbound packets with the same semantic families, now all classified at the MCU boundary. Discovery, transport acknowledgements and type-0x70/0x74 0d00 are request-derived; registration and channel-map frames are canned peer initiations. Type-0x70 selectors 0x13..0x16 are one-way task-2 bootstrap publications and 0x0a09 is a one-way post-completion follow-up. Seven type-0x51 packets form one command-0x22 DSP memory-image upload: v6 writes 247 words from 0x2206 and v5.01 writes 241 words from 0x2286. Type-0x1a publishes a reply-free 503-position GSM 900/DCS 1800 ARFCN bitmap; the coherent offline boot marks its dense sentinel source invalid and sends a zero channel set

NSE-8 v6.00 task 22 class 7 primitive 0x30 copies a four-byte serial-number/message-identifier header, a big-endian length and up to 0xaa bytes into a descriptor before posting task-5 MMI event 0x1859. An ordinary TS 03.41 page supplies exactly four header bytes plus an 84-byte DCS/page/content blob. The in-ROM producer census is empty and neither the closed MDIRCV packet switch nor the separate framed-session translator can publish class 7 primitive 0x30; the DSP-side publication mechanism remains capture-blocked and no scheduler injection is used

MAD2 DSPIF is a retained four-byte peer register; command halfword 0x0004 marks shared-control and L1 DSP work, while independent service-transport/shared-service timers and the observed ring-producer and service-pending triggers are required because command 4 does not accompany every ring commit

Product-owned native MAME I2C parts provide serial storage while MAD2 PUP bit-bangs SDA on 0x20.bit0, SCL on 0x20.bit3 and open-drain SDA direction on 0x24.bit0. NSE-8 uses a 24C128 with the documented page size and conservative 5 ms maximum write cycle; NSE-3 independently uses a 24C64

EEPROMSelX is unmapped after removal of an immutable-input alias with no hardware behavior. Five supported ROMs contain zero executable direct literal-derived accesses to the former 0xa00000..0xa03fff slice; dynamic pointers, the rest of the chip-select and future products remain outside the absence proof

The generated 3210 profile contains firmware-derived checksums and fallback data plus synthetic identity and working configuration fixtures; accepted bytes are test provisioning, not a factory EEPROM dump

The native PCD8544 device consumes organic firmware command/data transfers; both 3210 ROMs select endpoint 0x21, emit command prefix 24 40 80 and transfer a complete 504-byte image, while reset/electrical timing remains unvalidated

NV descriptor 0x0749 owns three 12-byte display profiles at EEPROM 0x18a8 in v6.00 and 0x18a0 in v5.01; equivalent ROM reset constructors at 0x29a802 and 0x296d6e explicitly author the same bytes 0..8 before committing variants 0..2. The generated EEPROM supplies those fields through normal NV loading, leaves constructor-unassigned bytes erased, and record-0 byte 5 becomes active slot 7 at 0x11fc87; a fully erased control leaves the panel blank

The paired 3210 ROMs complete 64 shared-word 0x00fe/0x0100 bootstrap exchanges and 3310 v6.39 completes 58 before the DSP HLE publishes words 0x0000..0x0004 ready. Product configuration owns that calibration; the 3310 clears its wait at 0x2bc96a without a firmware hook

3310 v6.39 reaches its deterministic idle frame with the shared DSP service, external-service and SIM devices plus standard CCONT channels 2/3/4 set to the evidenced normal-pack VBATT/BSI/BTEMP tuple 0x220/0x026/0x200. Its product-configured five-row keypad uses the shared direction AND NOT signal scan rule; physical Navi, Down and C cycles open the Phone book menu, enter and navigate its submenu, then return to the exact idle oracle. The same boot organically exchanges DSP self-test request 0x70/0x0d and completion 0x74/0x0d/0x00; no firmware hook or guessed reply is used

3330 v4.50 PPM E organically emits DSP type 0x70 payload 0d00 and requires its independently typed compact 0x74/0d00 completion through FIQ0. With that product contract it completes 64 bootstrap exchanges, fresh-PMM 12345/time/date editors, a save-state round trip, deterministic idle and physical navigation to Messages and back; omitting the completion reproduces CONTACT SERVICE. No oracle, firmware or RAM state is changed. Successful boot does not establish NHM-6 PCB signal identity

NHM-6 v4.50E organically publishes command-0x08 values 0x060b on physical Answer and 0x040a on physical End. Nokia's combined NHM-2/5/6 repair material identifies the common COBBA-GJP N100 audio boundary, whose documented codec SIO derives 1 MHz PCMDClk from 13 MHz / 13 and 8 kHz PCMSClk by /125 with a sign-extended 13-in-16 word. With an independently declared NHM-6 profile, preserved-PMM calls sustain bidirectional GSM-FR, FACCH stealing, bidirectional bad frames and concealment, four-phase SACCH coexistence, exact active-call save-state replay and clean teardown. No NHM-5 analogue route or gain is inherited

3410 v5.46 PPM E organically compacts its virgin PMM and emits DSP type 0x70 payload 0d00. Its explicit NHM-2 compact 0x74/0d00 completion crosses FIQ0 before the firmware exposes idle. Fresh-PMM save-state, physical Menu/End, Messages and exact return-to-idle gates pass with zero soft resets; NHM-2 does not inherit the NHM-6 product builder

NHM-2 v5.46E independently emits an autonomous band scan, publishes an ARFCN-1 candidate after a standards-shaped RSSI result, parses SI1-SI4, requests and accepts an assigned SDCCH, sends Location Updating through LAPDm, persists EF_LOCI, releases RR and returns to steady camp. Fresh and preserved PMM plus pre-acquisition and assigned-channel save/load gates pass. Access-barred, unattainable-RXLEV and mismatched Immediate Assignment request-reference fixtures do not reach Location Updating or mutate subscriber state

After organic NHM-2 registration, the generic paging scheduler derives the subscriber DRX group, delivers no-identity fill and one IMSI Paging Request Type 1, and firmware organically performs random access, assigned-SDCCH LAPDm Paging Response, RR release and return to PCH fill. Fresh and preserved PMM plus pre-page and assigned-exchange save/load gates pass. Wrong-group, unmatched, malformed and barred-cell fixtures produce no Paging Response or subscriber mutation

NHM-2 v5.46E organically recognizes an IMSI page, completes cipher/MM/CC setup, configures one TCH/F despite publishing Call Confirmed twice, drives the MAD2 buzzer, accepts physical Send and End, exchanges Connect Acknowledge and Release, confirms its independently observed 0x14 release CHANNEL_CONFIGURE parameter and returns to idle PCH. Analogue wiring remains outside this promotion

NHM-2 v5.46E organically publishes command-0x08 value 0x060b after physical Send and 0x040a during End. Combined NHM-2/5/6 repair material identifies COBBA-GJP N100 and its documented 1 MHz PCMDClk, 8 kHz PCMSClk and sign-extended 13-in-16 word. An independently typed NHM-2 profile sustains timed MAD2-COBBA PCM, bidirectional GSM-FR and non-silent downlink until TCH-owned teardown. The fitted analogue microphone and receiver routes remain unknown

CCONT watchdog data 0x00 removes the MAD2 digital baseband domain while CCONT and nonvolatile storage persist. A later physical charger edge exposes reset-cause bit 2, resets the CPU and attached MAD2 peripheral domain, and both 3210 v6.00 and v5.01 organically read the cause and VCHAR before settling in acting-dead mode 0x0005. Physical rail timing and battery/current dynamics remain unmodeled

The paired 3210 firmware routes early battery sampling to CCONT selector 0 and source-7 monitoring to selector 1. Both consume voltage thresholds; selector 1 uses voltage calibration, 1500/313 scaling and a 2100-unit undervoltage floor, although its internal NSE-8 mux remains unresolved. The service manual and conventional CCONT order identify selector 0 as Vb on RSSI, selector 2 as Vdc_out on VBAT, selector 3 as Vchout on BSI, selectors 4/5 as BTEMP/VCHAR, selector 6 as RF_temp on VCXOTEMP and selector 7 as EAD. The ADC helper exposes no conversion-ready bit, IRQ or delay operation, so TXP-synchronized physical conversion duration is not firmware-observable

A mapped GENSIO fixture loads CCONT watchdog register 5 with one second. Expiry resets the complete digital-baseband domain, restarts MAD2 clock initialization and preserves the exact pre-expiry CCONT status byte, including pending RTC sources and existing low reset flags. It does not use watchdog-data-zero rail-off and does not synthesize a new CCONT reset-cause bit

Five supported ROM controls contain byte-identical 18-entry CCONT descriptor tables: 90/90 entries map the same physical register vocabulary and each table has exactly two literal references. Separate organic two-second boots decode 933 phase-correct transactions and exercise 14 of 16 registers; longer RTC/alarm gates cover the remaining time fields. Registers 1, 4, 6 and 13 remain compatibility storage because traffic alone does not establish physical effects

A mapped controller fixture masks every upper CCONT source, creates simultaneous minute and alarm latches, and reads alarm bit 7 pending without an IRQ assertion. Clearing only mask bit 7 asserts the existing source through MAD2 IRQ2, after which firmware owns acknowledgement. The fixture changes controller registers only and does not write firmware state
